entries.title: Diddy Kong Racing
entries.definitive_edition: No single definitive edition: N64 is the main run; DS is a secondary remake for exclusive extras.

emulation.emulator: N64 emulator such as ares, Mupen64Plus, or Project64; Nintendo DS emulator for the secondary remake
emulation.notes: Use high internal resolution for N64 capture; use DS hardware/emulation only for the remake extras.
emulation.fidelity_ceiling: High-resolution N64 rendering for the primary; DS remake remains dual-screen handheld fidelity.

primary.version: Original Nintendo 64 release via high-resolution N64 emulation
primary.why: The Nintendo 64 original and the Nintendo DS remake differ: the N64 release preserves the original roster, including Banjo and Conker, while the DS version replaces them and adds DS-only modes/content, so N64 remains the main fidelity/authenticity route and DS is secondary.
primary.how_to_play: Play the N64 version through mature N64 emulation or original hardware for the main adventure. Then use the DS remake only to sample its exclusive tracks, custom-track/touch modes, online-era features, and replacement/new characters.

secondary.exclusive_content: DS remake with new modes, custom racetrack tools, online multiplayer, replacement/new characters, and other DS-specific changes.
secondary.what_to_play: Play the DS remake far enough to document the new modes/tools and roster changes; do not replace the N64 main playthrough with it.
secondary.why: It has exclusive modes/content but is not the most faithful or highest-fidelity version of the original adventure.

entries.remaster_caveats: Do not treat the DS remake as a straight upgrade: it changes roster/content and adds touch-centric features.

entries.remaster_caveats: NES and many home ports are historically important but not definitive; the Famicom/NES version omits the cement/pie factory stage.

primary.how_to_play: Play on DS/3DS hardware or a DS emulator; focus on built-in stages and local editor content because Nintendo Wi-Fi-era sharing is no longer dependable.

entries.remaster_caveats: Nintendo documented Wi-Fi sharing and contests for the original era; those online/community features are preservation caveats now.

emulation.notes: Use Wii U hardware for official play or Cemu for preservation and high-resolution display; online sharing features are no longer intact.

primary.version: Wii U eShop version
primary.why: Tipping Stars released on Wii U and Nintendo 3DS. Wii U is the higher-fidelity TV/GamePad route, though Miiverse/eShop service caveats apply.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Wii U version on hardware or verified Wii U emulation for the main game; use 3DS only if handheld play is preferred.

entries.remaster_caveats: Miiverse shutdown affected Workshop/Community sharing and stars, but main-game stages remain playable; Wii U/3DS eShop purchases are closed for new buyers.

primary.version: 2024 Nintendo Switch remake
primary.why: This is the distinct Switch remake of the 2004 GBA game, with modern 3D presentation and added modes/worlds.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Nintendo Switch release on Switch/Switch 2 hardware; archive the 2004 GBA version separately for the original design.

entries.remaster_caveats: Do not use this remake to overwrite the 2004 GBA entry: it adds modern presentation, co-op/casual/time-attack options, and new worlds.
